codex_claim_check: Checked against the Oct-7 source (build/sections/04-vertical.tex, 08-extraction.tex, 09-unit.tex, plus 02-classical, 06-pair, 07-theta, 10-center for the objects they refer to). The six files 02/04/07/08/09/10 are byte-identical between the Oct-3 and Oct-7 directories (diff), so the Oct-7 revision (history.md:25, citation removal) did not touch anything cited here. (1) Locations: all correct. `extraction:theta-implication` is 08-extraction.tex:28-42 (proof 44-1033, the entire section); `unit:simultaneous-jumps` is 09-unit.tex:252-265 (proof 267-388); `vertical:parity` is 04-vertical.tex:243-249 (proof 251-307), and the single-point acyclicity sentence Codex quotes is exactly 260-262: 'The simple-zero choices give one compact Selmer line from points, and its localization at either p-place is nonzero because the local logarithm has torsion kernel.' (2) 'Analytic horizontal zeros are identified with simultaneous Selmer jumps': partly accurate. The theta implication (08:28-42) gives ONE one-sided jump for ONE of V, V' (the companion twist) at a horizontal height-one prime containing b_w^0; the 'simultaneous' two-jump alternative is produced only in the unit theorem (09-unit.tex:429-434) by applying the two conjugate implications (w and w-bar) to a divisor F of both quotients, after (U_w)=(U_wbar) (09:97-125). (3) 'Divisors excluded via arithmetic tangent directions': accurate (09:252-388, using 04:336-499 lift test / obstruction span and 04:579-624 horizontal directions). (4) 'The arithmetic proof uses central acyclicity from a single point-generated Selmer line ... which fails for the seed's two-point plane': the location is right but the attribution is too coarse. The proof of the theta implication itself (08-extraction.tex:44-1033) does NOT use rank one, central acyclicity, or the simple-zero choices: its inputs are the open conditions of theta:test-point (07-theta.tex:193-257), the U(3,1) theta lift and Galois package imported from the Selmer-converse manuscript [C] (08:63, 326-327, 368, 495, 532, 683, 889, 975: [C] Lemmas 6.1, 6.4, 7.1-7.3, 8.5, 8.6, 8.8, 9.1-9.5, 9.7), absolute simplicity of V|G_L (08:742-744), and the unit rank of the CM biquadratic field L (08:857-865, a field fact). Rank one enters (a) upstream, in the EXISTENCE of the objects the proposition talks about: the auxiliary-field lemma is stated only for analytic rank r in {0,1} (02-classical.tex:116) and the tuple/residual-concentration eq. (1) (04:173-183) whose proof invokes vertical:parity (04:505-507); and (b) downstream, in unit:simultaneous-jumps, which needs 'every one-sided jump has even dimension' and 'generic fiber acyclic by (1)' (09:289-293). Codex's 'sections 8-9 arithmetic proof uses central acyclicity' therefore conflates the implication (rank-free as a proof, but about rank-one-only objects) with the exclusion (rank-one via parity). (5) 'Much closer to upper control': I disagree with the degree. What sections 8-9 deliver, if correct, is U_w in R^x (09:396-401), i.e. an anticyclotomic BDP/Heegner-type main-conjecture statement over an AUXILIARY Heegner-hypothesis field K=Q(sqrt D) with all primes dividing 2Np split (02:125-126); its seed-relevant output is only the central specialization 10-center.tex:34-54 / 115-141, which in rank one reads v_p(L_w(0)) = -2v_p(c_E)+2v_p(log P_K)+... (10:118-123) with 'every argument of v_p nonzero' (10:124). For the seed P_K is torsion (Gross-Zagier: L'(E/K,1)=0 since ord >= 2), so eq. (12) (06-pair.tex:281-290) gives B_w^{s=1}(0)=0 and the central comparison degenerates to 0=0; no bound on s_K=v_p#Sha(E/K) survives. (6) 'Retained question: prove the theta-zero-to-excess-jump implication for the actual divided rank-two source with all H^2 terms retained': mis-posed in two respects. The implication is a codimension-one (divisor) statement tested at interior points z_0 of a horizontal divisor over finite extensions of Q_p at characters of increasing p-conductor (07:193-199, 08:44-51); the seed's excess at the center is a point (t,u)=(0,0) of order >= 2 on which no divisor-level implication says anything (b_w^0 is not expected to lie in (t): tame twists of the central value are conductor-r Heegner sums). And the source b_w^0 is an anticyclotomic CM-point logarithm measure over K (06:255-290, eq. (10)-(12)), not a cyclotomic Kato element over Q, so it is not a counterpart of the lab's delta_p = A_p kappa(P1)+B_p kappa(P2) at all.
source_statement: Exact-BSD (Oct-7-2026), 08-extraction.tex:28-42, Proposition [Theta implication] \label{extraction:theta-implication}: 'Let p (frak) be a horizontal height-one prime of the deformation ring, with the auxiliary tuple conditions of Section~\ref{sec:theta}. If b_w^0 in p, then, over Frac(R/p), at least one of H^1_{prim,a}(K,V chi), H^1_{prim,a}(K,V' chi) is nonzero. Here a is one fixed side determined by the reciprocity convention of Section~\ref{sec:theta}. Replacing w by w-bar replaces a by its conjugate. Both alternatives use the scalar character of the determinant problem.' Definitions (08:12-26): R=Z_p[[t,u_1..u_d]] with t the anticyclotomic variable of K and u_j tame variables; V=V_pE, V'=V tensor chi_{D'} the companion twist; H^1_{prim,a} = degree-one group of the marked Selmer complex with strict condition at a in {w,w-bar}, full at the other p-place, unramified at fixed non-p places; 'jump' = that group nonzero. b_w^0 (06-pair.tex:267-278) is 'the first limiting series formed with F_0, without the non-p depletions', with B_w = unit.(b_w^0)^2 D (eq. 11) and central value B_w^{s=1}(0) = +/- c_E^{-2} log_{omega_E}(P_K)^2 P_p(1)^2 prod P_q(1)^2 (eq. 12, 06:281-290), P_K the conductor-one Hilbert-class Heegner trace. Standing hypotheses inherited from 02-classical.tex:115-137 (Lemma classical:auxiliary-fields): E/Q of ANALYTIC RANK r in {0,1}; D,D'<-4 coprime odd negative fundamental discriminants with every prime dividing 2Np split in Q(sqrt D) and Q(sqrt D'), (D/|D'|)=1, analytic ranks of E^D,E^{D'},E^{DD'} equal 1-r,1-r,r, L=Q(sqrt D,sqrt D') with L/F unramified CM and units {+-1}, L cap Q(E[p]) = Q; 'Both L(E/K,s) and L(E^{D'}/K,s) have a simple zero at s=1'; existence via the Goldfeld-density theorem of another OAI manuscript (02:103-113, references.tex:143-148, which in turn cites Smith arXiv:2503.17619v1). Section 4 (04-vertical.tex:13-16): 'both E/K and E^{D'}/K have rank one and finite Tate-Shafarevich group'; p odd, p splits completely in L. Companion statements: Lemma [Conjugate parity] 04:243-249: 'For an absolutely simple residual elliptic plane over K, each one-sided strict space above has even dimension. The same alternation statement holds on characteristic-zero localizations with unramified conditions at fixed non-p places and constant inertia action.' Proposition unit:simultaneous-jumps 09:252-265: 'The new tame directions can be chosen so that, for every such q, the following two loci have codimension at least two in Spec S_(q,y): (1) the locus where both one-sided primitive complexes for a single representation jump; (2) for each allocation of sides, the locus where one one-sided primitive complex for each of V_0,V_1 jumps. The old complexes are recovered on setting y=0, and the determinant and analytic specialization identities of Lemma pair:trace remain integral identities up to units.' Theorem unit:unit-comparison 09:396-401: 'The two quotients U_w are units. Their specialization with all artificial variables zero gives an integral unit comparison between the analytic series and strict determinant on the true anticyclotomic line.' Proof dependencies: theta:test-point (07:193-210, requires both primitive strict groups to vanish generically on the divisor as the contradiction hypothesis and nonvanishing of finitely many [C] denominators), theta:boundary-small (07:982-994, 'Assume b_w^0(z_0)=0'), [C] Prop 8.5 Galois representations for U(B+H) with Hodge-Tate weights (1-m_i-H_i, 2-m_i-H_i, 2-H_i, 1+H_i) (08:495-511), an ultraproduct coefficient field (08:182-194, 701-730), and 'strict unitary generic bounds on the unramified cuspidal roots' (08:906-910). Grade: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (unrefereed, AI-generated); BSD family has no Lean entry; depends on OAI manuscripts [C] (Selmer converse, Oct-7 revision of a Sept-24 version), [B] (two-primary, Oct 6) and [Goldfeld] (Oct 7), none withdrawn per history.md.
what_it_would_need: To serve any seed obligation the lead needs ALL of the following, none supplied by the manuscript and none deducible from it: (N1) A rank-two CENTRAL leading-term theorem, not a divisor statement: for E over an auxiliary Heegner-hypothesis K' (all primes dividing 2Np split; the lab's K=Q(sqrt -7) is excluded since 3, 2243, 5843 are inert, 02:125-126 and 04:14-16), with d = dim ker(E(K') tensor Q_p -> E(K'_w) tensor Q_p) >= 1, a formula identifying v_p of the order-2d leading coefficient of B_w^{s=1}(t) at t=0 with a derived determinant (anticyclotomic/derived p-adic height regulator on that kernel) plus the index, torsion and Tamagawa terms of 10-center.tex:38-53 and minus s_K. This is the rank-two BDP/derived-Gross-Zagier object already recorded by the lab as PRECISE_OBSTRUCTION in the Aristotle returns; sections 8-9 contribute nothing to it because their output (U_w a unit) specializes at the seed's center to 0=0 (eq. 12 with P_K torsion). (N2) Replacement of the rank-one step in vertical:parity (04:260-266) by a proof of GENERIC acyclicity of the strict-at-w/full-at-w-bar complex over Z_p[[t,u]] for the seed over K' -- i.e. cotorsion of the tame-extended BDP Selmer group. This is the only place sections 4 and 9 use rank one, and generic (not central) acyclicity is what the alternating-matrix parity argument (04:291-297) and 09:289-293 need. Published candidates (Heegner-point Kolyvagin systems; Lambda-adic BDP cotorsion results) carry their own hypotheses (p good, rho-bar irreducible/surjective, Heegner hypothesis for K', p prime to class number, sometimes p ordinary) and would have to be source-checked prime by prime; for the seed the Heegner hypothesis forces rank E(K') >= 3 with E^D of odd rank >= 1 (Codex's -23 remark), so the central kernel has dimension >= 2 and no manuscript-style 'one line from points' exists. Supplying N2 only restores the §9 exclusion; it does not produce N1. (N3) A companion-twist construction for analytic rank >= 2: the auxiliary-field lemma (02:115-137) is stated for r in {0,1} and its parity bookkeeping (1-r,1-r,r) and the pair identity X(E)+X(E^D)=0 (10:143-165, 'For every elliptic curve of analytic rank zero or one') have no rank-two meaning; the descent step of the theta implication (08:1011-1028, Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} V = V + V') needs a companion whose one-sided groups are controlled. (N4) Independent verification and grading of the [C] import chain the proof rests on (08:63-1033 cites [C] in at least eleven places), of the ultraproduct limit argument (08:182-194, 701-730), and of the Ramanujan-type bound at 08:906-910; K-GRADE caps all of this at IMPORTED_PREPRINT. (N5) For the lab's actual derivative target (delta_p, m_p - w_p <= 1 at good p >= 5 outside {19,59,487}): a bridge from the CYCLOTOMIC Kato object over Q to an ANTICYCLOTOMIC CM-point measure over K'; the manuscript has no such bridge (its Q-side single-curve comparison in §5 is a one-sided inequality that explicitly 'does not require the normalized coordinate to be a unit', 01-introduction.tex:186-189, and uses no theta implication). Without N5 the retained question 'theta-zero to excess-jump for the actual divided rank-two source' has no source to apply to.

(1)(b) over Z_p[[t,u]] for a fixed p (04:173-183), not uniform in p. Named remainder 59, 487 -- no (same reasons; also these are excluded from the lab's derivative domain for separate reasons). 2243, 5843 -- no: multiplicative primes inert in the lab's K; the manuscript needs p odd and split in L (04:14, 06:5) and K' with all of 2Np split. 4547 -- no (additive; it would have to split in K', and nothing in §§8-9 addresses an additive p). ORDER9 -- no (no bound on #Sha at any p). Q36 -- no: the exact-center machinery of §10 degenerates to 0=0 at the seed's center (P_K torsion in eq. 12) and the archimedean rank-two comparison is untouched. Plectic lemma TH at 5843 -- no: TH is the first derivative at the trivial character of a level-raised theta element in the definite (Gross point) setting with p=5843 inert in Q(sqrt -7); the theta implication concerns zeros of a Heegner-logarithm measure along divisors with p split. Cost reduction -- no: the lab's K-route needs nonvanishing of a Gross-packet second moment M_2(p) at a point (definite quaternion algebra of discriminant 3.2243.5843); a divisor-level implication in the indefinite case neither certifies nor cheapens a point value. new_observation: NEW-1 (hypothesis Codex overlooked): the rank-one hypothesis is not only in vertical:parity; it is in the STATEMENT scope of the auxiliary-field lemma, 02-classical.tex:116 'Let E/Q have conductor N and analytic rank r in {0,1}', which creates the fields K, K'=Q(sqrt D'), L, the companion V', and the simple zeros that every later object presupposes; and in 02:188-194, where the one-dimensional compact Selmer line over K with nonzero local logarithm is asserted BEFORE section 4. For the seed (analytic rank >= 2) the lemma is vacuous, so the theta implication has no admissible 'auxiliary tuple conditions' to be stated under, independently of what happens in vertical:parity. NEW-2 (what the rank-one step really proves): vertical:parity and unit:simultaneous-jumps consume only GENERIC acyclicity of the one-sided complex (04:256-267 'It is generically acyclic. To check this last assertion, specialize centrally'; 09:291-292 'Its generic fiber is acyclic by (1)'). Central acyclicity is the manuscript's route to it, not the needed property; Codex's 'fails for the seed's two-point plane' is right about the route and should not be read as a claim that the one-sided complex is generically non-acyclic for the seed. The correct replacement target is a Lambda-cotorsion theorem for the tame-extended BDP Selmer group (N2), a literature object with its own hypotheses, not a new 'reduced complex' construction. NEW-3 (point versus divisor): for the seed the analytic series itself vanishes at the center, B_w^{s=1}(0)=0 by eq. (12) because P_K is torsion when ord_{s=1}L(E/K,s) >= 2, while b_w^0 is not expected to lie in the height-one prime (t) (its restriction to t=0 is the family of conductor-r Heegner sums over the tame variables). The seed's 'excess' therefore sits at a closed point of codimension two in Spec Z_p[[t,u]], exactly the codimension the §9 exclusion is designed to IGNORE (09:253-255 'codimension at least two'). The manuscript's architecture is built to discard precisely the locus where the seed lives. NEW-4 (a section closer to the lab's target than §§8-9): the lab's delta_p is a cyclotomic Kato object over Q; the manuscript's cyclotomic/Q-side material is §5 (single:kato-calibration 05-single.tex:213-297 and single:period-law 05:299-340, already noted by Codex as normalization sources) and the Q-side residual concentration of §4 (04:28-29 'Over Q include p and all bad primes'; 04:530-533 'Over Q the dual strict vanishing gives H^2=0 for the primal full complex. Its Euler characteristic is -1, so it has one residual degree-one line'). The Q-side residual line count (-1 Euler characteristic, one line) is the manuscript's rank-one anchor on the cyclotomic side; for the seed the primal residual degree-one space has dimension >= 2 from the two saturated points at t=0 (tors = Z/2), so eq. (1)(a) 'G tensor R_(p) is a free line in degree one' (04:178) is false for the seed without tame deformation killing the point directions, which cannot be done at t=0,u=0. This is the same obstruction as L2's residual concentration and is independent of the theta machinery. NEW-5 (thin places in the manuscript's own proof, relevant to K-GRADE): (i) the theta implication's proof passes through an ultraproduct coefficient field K_cal with 'filter-large set of stages' and relabelling (08:182-194), and the corner-module construction uses henselizations of ultraproducts of Hecke orders (08:701-730); no effective content is retained; (ii) 08:906-910 invokes 'strict unitary generic bounds on the unramified cuspidal roots' placing Frobenius sizes 'strictly between Q and Q^2' -- a Ramanujan-type input for U(3,1) whose exact source is not cited in this section; (iii) the companion-twist existence rests on the Goldfeld-density OAI manuscript (02:103-113) which cites Smith's 2025 arXiv preprint as the Selmer-distribution input (references.tex:184-188), a preprint-to-preprint-to-preprint chain; (iv) the proof of the theta implication cites at least eleven distinct lemmas/propositions of [C] (08:63, 327, 368, 441, 495, 532, 546, 672, 683, 889, 975), so its correctness is not separable from the Selmer-converse manuscript. NEW-6 (version check): sections 02/04/07/08/09/10 are byte-identical between the Oct-3 and Oct-7 directories; the Oct-7 change (history.md:25) is a citation removal only, so the Oct-6 Claude audit's reading of §9 'in part' and this reading concern the same text.
risks: Risk of over-reading Codex's 'much closer to upper control': the phrase suggests a near-miss for an excess-content bound; in fact the mechanism yields an anticyclotomic main-conjecture-type unit over an auxiliary field whose central specialization is 0=0 for the seed, and the seed's excess lies in the codimension-two locus the argument discards. Risk of pursuing the 'retained question' as stated: there is no 'actual divided rank-two source' in the manuscript's sense (anticyclotomic CM-point measure over a Heegner-hypothesis K'); constructing one is the K-route's Gross/Heegner machinery, and over any Heegner-hypothesis K' the seed has rank >= 3, which enlarges rather than removes the central kernel. Risk of mis-grading a rank-free-looking statement: the proposition's text has no rank hypothesis, but its objects (auxiliary tuple, companion V', b_w^0) exist only under 02:116; quoting it as 'rank-independent' would be a K-RANK2 error. Risk of double-counting: this lead overlaps L2 (same eq. (1) residual-concentration anchor) and the Oct-6 audit's §7-8 'position-cut' remark; none of the three supplies a seed theorem. Risk of import creep: adopting N2 from published Kolyvagin-system literature would introduce hypotheses (good p, image, class number, Heegner hypothesis for a new K') that must be checked per prime and that exclude 2243, 4547, 5843 outright. Grading risk: everything here is IMPORTED_PREPRINT with dependence on three other unrefereed OAI manuscripts; no Lean coverage for family 002. Remaining uncertainty in this assessment: I did not re-derive the [C] theta-lift inputs or the §5 single-curve calibration, so 'the theta-implication proof is rank-free' is a statement about which hypotheses the text invokes, not a verification that the proof is correct.
verdict_rationale_short: Codex located the rank-one step correctly but rated the lead closer to the lab's target than the source supports: the implication is divisor-level, anticyclotomic over an auxiliary Heegner-hypothesis field whose Heegner point is torsion for the seed (central value 0 by eq. 12), its objects exist only under the analytic-rank-<=1 auxiliary-field lemma (02:116), and its downstream product (U_w a unit) cannot reach a central valuation in rank two without the derived leading-term formula the lab already records as PRECISE_OBSTRUCTION. Hence DISAGREE_LESS_USABLE; obligation served: none.
